_comment: Config for the weekly sharded mutation run.
SCOPE: RunnerCore only -- the one target proven end to end. The 2026-08-18
pilot ran exactly this code and scored 69% (88 killed, 39 survived, zero build
errors) over four of its files. It is also the code where a survivor matters
most: one grading core compiled natively AND to wasm, pinned by
Tests/Fixtures/output-contract.json. ~1,600 LOC, ~266 mutants, 3 shards of
~30 minutes.
WHY NOT MORE, YET. Widening to Core + Worker aborted every shard of run 2:
Muter runs the suite UNMUTATED first and refuses to mutate anything if that
baseline is red, and the baseline was red with `Suite WorkerTests failed with 2
issues` -- identically on all ten shards, independent of their file sets. Widen
again only after a run at this scope is green, one target at a time.
--skip WorkerTests/ removes exactly the 48 tests of the WorkerTests SUITE, not
the 343 of the WorkerTests MODULE: ids read `WorkerTests.WorkerTests/...` for
the suite and `WorkerTests.CppNativeGradingTests/...` for its siblings, so the
trailing slash discriminates. That keeps the 295 sibling tests that actually
cover RunnerCore -- notebook extraction, script classification, the R and Lua
runtimes -- while dropping the suite that holds the timing-sensitive sandbox and
timeout tests and spawns concurrent worker daemons. Running those in one process
beside CoreTests on a 2-core runner is a configuration nothing else exercises:
CI runs the targets as separate jobs, and on a laptop the interpreter-dependent
tests skip, which is why the same command passes locally with 760 green.
--skip ZipProcessEnvironmentTests is not strictly needed while only RunnerCore is
in scope -- it reads Sources/Core files, which are not mutated here, so no
preamble reaches them. It stays because it WILL be needed the moment Core is
added: Muter writes `import class Foundation.ProcessInfo` into every file it
mutates before the baseline runs, and that suite scans those files for
`Process(` constructions. The general rule: a test asserting on the TEXT of a
file under mutation cannot coexist with mutation, and has no mutants worth
killing anyway.
-Xswiftc -no-warnings-as-errors IS LOAD-BEARING. The package builds with
.treatAllWarnings(as: .error), and RemoveSideEffects deletes the USE of a
binding, leaving `let x = ...` unused -- a warning, therefore an error,
therefore a copy that does not compile and a shard that yields zero mutants.
APIServer is excluded permanently, not pending: 94k LOC, ~15,700 mutants that
must be graded by APITests, ~1,712h serial -- ~96% of the tree's cost for its
least informative mutants. Triage scales with SURVIVORS, and a report nobody can
read is worse than none because it looks like coverage.
